title: Find the Black Swan
coreMove: Keep probing past the visible deal until the hidden fact that changes leverage appears.
sourcePressure: The source ties the close to unknown unknowns, hidden leverage, information asymmetry, and breakthrough facts that can overturn even strong bargaining logic.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must not treat random details as black swans, make intuition mystical, or suggest profiling can replace disciplined discovery.

hook: A gut feeling solves the negotiation
A surprising fact appears from nowhere
counterintuition: The hidden thing is the deal

exampleSpecs.domain: rural clinic merger negotiation with a hospital network
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic board chair trying to understand why the network suddenly softened its terms
exampleSpecs.stakes: the board may give up governance rights without seeing the network's hidden state-license deadline
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chair asks what happens if the deal is not signed this quarter and discovers the network needs the clinic's license address to keep a service line open
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a state license renewal envelope half-visible under a merger binder tab

exampleSpecs.domain: manufacturer negotiating with a sole-source sensor supplier
exampleSpecs.audience: a production director trying to learn why the supplier resists a modest volume increase
exampleSpecs.stakes: a product launch may stall unless the hidden bottleneck is found
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director asks what would make the added volume easy, and the supplier reveals the limiting factor is a calibration bench, not raw parts
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tray of tiny sensors waiting under a magnifying inspection lamp

exampleSpecs.audience: an orchestra manager negotiating with an agent over a fee that suddenly seems rigid
exampleSpecs.stakes: the concert may be canceled if the manager misses the non-fee condition driving the agent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager asks what makes this date difficult, uncovering that the conductor needs a rehearsal recording for a visa dossier
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a conductor's marked score lying beside an unsigned artist agreement

exampleSpecs.audience: a grocer bargaining with a warehouse owner over renewal terms
exampleSpecs.stakes: the grocer may overpay if she misses the warehouse's hidden vacancy problem
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the grocer predicts that price is the only issue, then asks what happens to the adjacent freezer bay and learns the owner needs her tenancy to qualify for a utility rebate
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a frost line tracing the edge of an empty freezer bay door

exampleSpecs.audience: an athletic director trying to understand a sponsor's sudden insistence on naming rights
exampleSpecs.stakes: the school may reject money it needs because it misses the sponsor's hidden grant-matching requirement
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director pauses before refusing naming rights and asks what internal deadline the sponsor is trying to satisfy, revealing a grant match that changes the package
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a neon arena rendering pinned over a spreadsheet of sponsorship tiers

exampleSpecs.audience: an operator negotiating with nearby growers who oppose a permit expansion
exampleSpecs.stakes: the facility may abandon expansion when the hidden objection is truck timing, not odor
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the operator reviews how asking what would make the expansion harmless revealed that growers feared harvest-road congestion during two October weeks
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a harvest-road map smudged with soil beside an odor-monitoring report

skillTargets: distinguish black swans from random details
ask questions that uncover hidden constraints or leverage
analyze how new information changes bargaining power
evaluate whether a discovery is decisive enough to alter the deal

tryThisNowSpec: For one stuck negotiation, ask what changes for the other side if nothing happens by a specific date; listen for the constraint that was not visible in the stated terms.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
